decisions.statement: The command's own name is refused in the program's place alone.
A name the runner starts a process by is a launching call.
The program a runner is handed is the first word of the list that runner takes.
A name is judged by what that name spells rather than by where it was taken from.
No path a launching call names is read.
A name bound to a literal at the top of the file is read as that literal.
A path built by joining is read through to the literals the path joins.
A string shown to a reader is not a call.
A test file is judged as every other file is judged.
A process a program starts to outlive its caller is not the call this rule refuses.
No use of the command from code is kept as permitted.
A name built as the code runs is not seen.

definition: the rule refusing a call that runs the akasha command from inside akasha
